identity.title: Sam Harris vs. Jonathan Haidt. Sam and Jonathan debate religion and morality.
identity.dateBasis: The official episode page identifies Evolving Minds, episode 31, March 9, 2016. At source 76:46 the speakers locate their conversation at the beginning of March before the Trump–Clinton election; this contradicts the uploader’s 2018 label.

content.captionCaution: Both speakers explicitly identify as atheists and naturalists. Harris grants nonbelief aspects of religion, social benefits, evolved constraints and multiple good lives; Haidt grants that doctrines matter, rejects fundamentalism, rejects an inference from evolution directly to moral goodness, supports institutional reason and agrees that more flourishing is better other things equal. The live dispute concerns explanatory adequacy and normative sufficiency, not God’s existence or whether suffering matters. Do not impose denial of conceded claims on either side. The recording starts during the religion discussion and continues to the episode close; assess only the complete uploaded material, not a claimed complete original episode. Their substantially aligned late campus/political discussion is context; select any genuinely motion-relevant argument according to its actual adopted burden, never invent opposition. Caption errors are not participant errors. Below-high attribution requires audio checks; repeated clear wording is not proof of voice attribution. Stop if an additional substantive speaker or material source gap is discovered.
